text: He had chosen a Boeing 727 on purpose. He understood its one unusual feature better than most passengers ever would.

text: The 727 carried a set of stairs built into its tail, under the fuselage. A door you could open in flight.

text: His instructions to the cockpit were unusual. Fly toward Mexico City. Stay low, under ten thousand feet, flaps lowered, landing gear down.
provenance: His instructions to the cockpit were unusual enough that the pilots had to push back on some of them.
Fly toward Mexico City. Stay low, under ten thousand feet. Keep the speed down, the wing flaps lowered, the landing gear hanging in the wind. And leave the rear staircase, the aft airstair, unlocked.

text: He asked for four parachutes, not one. If an innocent person might jump too, the chutes could not be rigged to fail.
provenance: And four parachutes. Two main chutes, two reserves.
By asking for four, he made the authorities believe he might force one of the crew or passengers to jump alongside him.
And if an innocent person might be going out that door, the parachutes could not be rigged, could not be sabotaged, could not be packed to fail.

text: Nothing about it was improvised. He had quietly guaranteed himself working equipment, without ever saying so. That is not panic. That is planning.
